funding.supported_assets_note: Virtual Visa card issued by Third National for Exa Labs SAS, funded from a self-custodial wallet on the Exactly Protocol. Two 'Pay Mode' settings: 'Pay now' — 'the value of every purchase you make will be directly deducted from your stored assets'; 'Installments' — the app borrows the amount 'from Exactly Protocol's fixed-rate lending markets', converts it to USD and pays the merchant, 'The interest rate is fixed and determined at the time of the transaction'. Card terms: the Exactly Protocol 'extends credit to you'. Supported blockchains in the card terms: Ethereum, Polygon, Optimism, Arbitrum. Purchases are USD-denominated; installments repaid in USDC.

credit_terms.liquidation_risk: The card terms list a 'Liquidation fee (Reserved)' and state 0% interest on purchases, while the help centre describes installment purchases as loans from Exactly Protocol's fixed-rate markets with a rate 'determined at the time of the transaction' and a possible origination fee 'included in the interest you pay on the installments'. No APR figure, loan-to-value, collateral factor or liquidation mechanism is published on the pages read.

eligibility.nationality_restrictions_note: Card terms: 'You attest that you are not a United States citizen' and the card 'is intended for those outside of the United States'; cardholders must not be blocked or sanctioned (OFAC). Use limited to personal, family or household purposes.
eligibility.usage_note: Allowed list = 'Eligible countries' of the help article 'How can I get my Exa Card?' (48 countries) plus the United States for the 31 states it lists (AL, AK, AR, CA, CO, CT, FL, HI, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, ME, MA, MI, MN, MT, NE, NH, NJ, NY, NC, OK, PA, SC, TX, UT, VA, WV, WY). Nigeria, South Africa and Sri Lanka are 'subject to approval' ('Issuance there may not be available') and are left unlisted. Excluded list = union of that article's 17 'Ineligible countries' and the 31-country 'List of prohibited countries' article. No EEA, UK or Swiss country appears on the eligible list; Bulgaria and Croatia are explicitly prohibited. Cards cannot be used in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Ukraine or Venezuela.

kyc.thresholds_note: No threshold: 'After downloading the Exa App, going through KYC, and adding funds, a credit card is created.' Referral terms: 'mandatory KYC'.
kyc.stages_note: Account creation then KYC before the virtual card can be requested ('validation' step 'won't take more than 3 minutes'); funds must be in the account to enable the card. Documents required and verification provider are not stated on any page read.

access.note: No membership or subscription is mentioned on any page read; the card is requested in-app after KYC and funding. Not confirmed as free — see fees.

fees.conditions: No issuance price for the virtual card is stated on the fees article, the card terms or the 'How can I get my Exa Card?' article.
No annual or monthly fee row was found on the fees article or in the card terms' fee table; absence is not treated as free.
Funding = transferring assets to the user's self-custodial wallet; no deposit fee is stated. Network gas and any on-ramp partner fees are not documented on the pages read.

Fees article: 'has a 1.5% FX fee (foreign transaction fee) included in the currency rate' on non-USD transactions. Card terms fee table: 'Foreign Exchange Fee (non-USD): 1.5%', 'Foreign transaction fees: up to 1.5%' and a separate 'Cross Border Fee: 1%' whose application (cumulative or alternative) is not explained.

'$1 + 0.65% per transaction' via contactless (NFC) ATMs with the card in Apple Wallet or Google Pay and the in-app PIN; 'Some ATMs may charge more'. Limits: 'Up to $250 per withdrawal', 'Max 4 withdrawals per day'.

Installment mode: 'We may charge an origination fee whenever you make a loan', amount not stated, 'included in the interest you pay on the installments'. Card terms: returned payment fee $0.00; liquidation fee '(Reserved)'; cash advances and balance transfers not available.

limits.note: 'Up to $250 per withdrawal', 'Max 4 withdrawals per day'.

editorial.summary: Virtual Visa card from the Exa App (Exactly Protocol), issued by Third National for Exa Labs SAS, that spends against crypto held in a self-custodial wallet: 'pay now' deducts each purchase from stored assets, 'installments' borrows at a fixed rate from Exactly Protocol's lending markets. 1.5% FX on non-USD payments, ATM $1 + 0.65% via phone wallets, no published cashback. Eligible in about 48 countries across Latin America, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific plus 31 US states; not offered in the EEA or UK. Issuance, subscription and deposit costs and the installment APR are not published on the pages read.
good_for: Residents of Latin America, Africa or Asia-Pacific who hold assets on Ethereum L2s and want to spend without selling
Users comfortable with a self-custodial, protocol-based card and installment borrowing at a rate shown in-app
not_for: Residents of the EEA, UK or Switzerland — not on the eligible list (Bulgaria and Croatia explicitly prohibited)
Anyone who needs a published APR, loan-to-value or liquidation rule before borrowing
Cashback seekers — no rewards are published
watch_outs: Official pages contradict each other: 0% interest in the card terms vs fixed-rate installment loans with a possible origination fee in the help centre; a 'not a United States citizen' attestation vs 31 eligible US states; 17 vs 31 excluded countries.
Installment purchases are loans against your collateral on the Exactly Protocol; APR, LTV and liquidation mechanics are not on any page read ('Liquidation fee (Reserved)').
FX 1.5% plus a separate 1% 'Cross Border Fee' row in the terms whose interaction is unexplained — up to 2.5% may apply on foreign purchases.
Issuance, annual and deposit fees are not published; nothing here is modelled as free.
Virtual card only; ATM withdrawals need Apple Wallet / Google Pay and a contactless ATM ($250 per withdrawal, 4 a day).
Help-centre articles are dated by author line only ('Updated over a week ago'); the fee article dates from October 2024.
